title: August and the Postcard
author: Y. M. Dravenmoor
blurb: Odile Zhou, a marine biologist counting turtles instead of heartbreaks, swears the heart is a muscle like any other: trainable, containable. Then the anonymous pen-pal assignment pairs enemies instead of strangers — and he is pulled straight into the middle of it. To get through this, he must risk the whole heart instead of lending pieces before the bakery lease runs out.
style: wry first-person narration with emotional depth
